same_basis_candidates.why_it_applies: Singapore Food Regulations reg 31(5) (informal consolidation in force from 30 January 2026; cadmium paragraph amended S 195/2011 and S 695/2021) names 'molluscs or dried mushrooms' (1 ppm), 'seaweed' (2 ppm) and 'cocoa, cocoa products or salt' (0.5 ppm) and puts every other food at 0.2 ppm; crustaceans are not molluscs, so the crustacean constituent of this row falls in 'other food' at 200 ug/kg. Food-content basis (product as sold or imported), status 'maximum level', not gated. The bivalve constituent stays at the Singapore molluscs row (1000), which is looser than the derived value.

Uruguay Reglamento Bromatologico Nacional section 1.2.14 general limit 'solid foods in general except categories with particular limits' (0.2 mg/kg, statutory, food-content basis). The register carries no particular Uruguayan cadmium row for crustaceans, bivalves or any fishery product (its only other Cd rows are ceramic migration rows), so on the register's own evidence the fallback reaches fresh and frozen shellfish. Conditional: if Uruguay has internalised MERCOSUR GMC Res 12/2011 (crustaceans 500, bivalve molluscs 2000) as the 'particular limits' the fallback yields to, this row does not bind; the register and regulation page cannot show that.

cells.reason: The anchor itself is valid: eu2023_cd_crustaceans_500 (EU 2023/915 Annex I row 'Crustaceans', 0.50 mg/kg wet weight, muscle meat of appendages and abdomen, in force) is a content ML on a content cell and covers the crustacean constituent of 'Shellfish (crustaceans and bivalve molluscs, not canned)'; the bivalve constituent is governed by the EU 'Bivalve molluscs' row at 1.0 mg/kg (shown on regulations/eu-2023-915-cadmium but absent from the register), so 500 is the strictest EU member value and its application to bivalves is strictest-member precaution, not the bivalve ML. Confirmation fails on condition (d): Singapore reg 31(5) carves out 'molluscs or dried mushrooms' at 1 ppm and leaves crustaceans in 'other food' at 0.2 ppm = 200 ug/kg, a same-basis, non-gated, in-force sovereign content ML stricter than the derived value for the crustacean constituent, and Uruguay's 'solid foods in general' 200 nominally reaches shellfish because the register holds no particular Uruguayan fishery Cd row. Excluded as not covering this form: VN QCVN 8-2 'Aquatic products' 50 (the same table's specific 'Crustaceans' 500 and 'Bivalve mollusks' 2000 rows govern), and every other same-basis fishery row (CN GB 2762-2025, IN, MERCOSUR/PY, MA, GSO, CR, GY, PA, FJ, VN, HK, SG molluscs) is 500 or looser; Thailand has no crustacean or residual Cd row and falls back to Codex CXS 193, which sets no crustacean Cd ML. Blind value 200 for the row under the strictest-member rule the row already relies on; the alternative is to split crustaceans (200 if SG is admitted, else 500) from bivalves (1000) and to document any exclusion of residual catch-all rows from the pool.
